chunks: And from him (Al-Hurr al-Amili) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a mukatab (a slave who has agreed to pay a specific sum for his freedom) who dies after having paid part of his manumission contract, and he has a son from a concubine, and he left wealth, he (the Imam) said: 'His son pays the remainder of his manumission, and he is freed, and he inherits what remains (of the wealth).'

key_terms.جَارِيَةٍ: A female concubine or slave woman.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom in installments.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission contract or the agreed-upon price for the slave's freedom.

ai.seo_question: What happens to a deceased mukatab's remaining debt and estate if he leaves a son?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal mechanism of *kitabah* by establishing that the son assumes the father's remaining debt to secure his emancipation, thereby transforming the father from a slave into a free heir. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that manumission is a prerequisite for inheritance, ensuring the deceased mukatab’s estate is distributed among free heirs rather than remaining with the master. It highlights the intergenerational responsibility in fulfilling manumission contracts, a key concept in Usuli fiqh regarding the status of mixed-status families.
